item.title: ML4QGIS: machine learning inside QGIS
item.description:
ML4QGIS (Machine Learning for QGIS) brings machine learning for image classification and regression into QGIS, so geospatial analysts can train and apply models without writing code.

  • Available in the official QGIS plugin repository (version 0.4.0, August 2026), with more than 6,000 downloads.
  • Open source under GPL-3.0 on GitHub.
  • Introduced at FOSS4GNL 2025 and used in the FOSS4G 2026 workshop GeoAI Level Up, including YOLO object detection inside ML4QGIS.

Feedback, issues and pull requests are welcome.

item.title: Benchmarking AI agents for GIS
item.description:
AI agents are starting to operate GIS software on their own. How reliable are they on real geospatial tasks?

I lead the design of a benchmark that evaluates AI agents on geospatial tasks in QGIS. The benchmark questions are openly available on Zenodo.

item.title: Solar panels and electricity access from space
item.description:
• Built a YOLOv11 object-detection pipeline that detects solar panels in satellite imagery.
  • Developed Python and Google Earth Engine workflows on VIIRS night-light imagery to identify rural areas lacking electricity access.
  • Built ML-ready training datasets from multi-temporal satellite imagery and coordinated the field data collection used to label them.

item.title: Mapping public urban green spaces with open data
item.description:
Equitable access to green and public space is part of SDG 11.7, but up-to-date maps of public green spaces are rare, and existing approaches often depend on proprietary software.

This work builds a fully reproducible workflow using only Sentinel-2 imagery, OpenStreetMap data and open-source Python libraries, covering data acquisition, preprocessing, deep learning and evaluation.

Read the paper: City and Environment Interactions (2026).

item.title: Machine learning for pollen prediction
item.description:
Smart Monitoring for a Changing Climate: Machine Learning in Pollen Prediction.

Spatiotemporal machine learning to predict pollen, building on my work with Random Forest, Mixed Effects Random Forest, Prophet and SVM models for climate and Earth-system prediction. Presented at the NWO NAC conference (2026).
